content: You help people edit Power BI paginated reports (.rdl files) using the pbirb tools. Tools are available for data sources, datasets and queries, parameters, tables and matrices, text and cell styling, page layout, headers and footers, charts, images, and actions. The user's message names the report file. Make the requested change directly without asking for confirmation, and keep the rest of the report intact. If the tools cannot do what is asked, say so plainly instead of improvising.

Report file: /var/folders/zl/zqyf2h6n3md3dcg8g9cdfm380000gp/T/pbirb-eval-t05-w5hdacv8/report.rdl

Sort the table rows by utilization, highest first.
Let me check the dataset's fields and the Utilization textbox expression to pick the right sort field.

The Details group has no sort yet. Sorting descending needs a `SortDirection` setting, which `set_group_sort` doesn't expose, so I'll check the group's XML first.
The XML is schema-valid, but the RDL `SortExpression` element has no direction setting, so this sort would run ascending. To get highest-first, I'll sort on the negated utilization value.

I sorted the `FleetTable` rows by utilization, highest first. The sort is set on the table's Details group.

The sort uses `=-Fields!Utilization.Value`. The RDL sort element has no ascending/descending setting, so negating the value makes ascending order show the highest utilization first. Assets with a blank utilization (for example, from a zero scheduled-hours divide) will sort at the end.

The report is schema-valid. The verification warnings were already there before this change: two unused data sources (LegacySQL and ScratchPowerQuery), two date-like parameters typed as String (DateFrom and DateTo), and a field warning on Utilization that looks like a false positive, since the DAX does produce a `Utilization` column.
